Before the conflict started and even afterwards, a considerable number of people left Sarajevo via Ilidza. The Serbian Army and civilian authorities did not prevent anyone from leaving. Further, higher commands issued orders to facilitate unhindered passage of humanitarian aid convoys. These were adhered to even though on several occasions whilst carrying out routine checks it was discovered that the convoys contained prohibited and undeclared goods. With regard to the sniping incident near the junction of Nikola Demonja and Bulevar AVNOJ in Dobrinja, Svetozar Guzina states that the distance between the alleged point and the alleged place where it struck is greater than the range that can be successfully attained by any sniper rifle in the VRS arsenal. There is no optical visibility between the alleged place of firing and the place of the incident. With regard to the sniping incident in Djure Jaksica street, Svetozar Guzina states that the place of the alleged incident was behind the first line and that it was not logical to assume the presence of civilians in this location. [Interpretation] That would be the summary. I'd just like to put a few questions to you. In your statement here, you said that you never issued an order to fire at civilians, and that your subordinates never issued such orders. Nevertheless, did it happen that civilians would get killed on both sides?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How would that happen? How do you explain that if it was not on orders?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: At any rate, it wasn't on orders. It is a fact that there were civilian casualties on both sides. However, I can say freely that this is collateral damage on both sides. Civilians who happened to be on the front line, no one wanted to kill them. They simply happened to be there because fire that had been opened was not individual fire. It was automatic gunfire. There was a lot of bullet dispersion on both sides, and therefore civilian casualties could not be avoided. As far as the Serb side is concerned, at least in my commanding the 1st Battalion, civilians were ordered not to go to their homes. It was forbidden. But simply people went to their homes to see their houses, to see their property, to see whether everything was in proper order, and that is how quite a few ended up getting killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The armies in your area, were they properly dressed? Could you make a distinction between them and civilians?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: No, certainly not. The first year, year and a half, we all wore camouflage. Some people had military uniforms of the TO defence, and quite a few of us simply had tracksuits, trainers, civilian clothing, and we went to the front line to carry out our duties dressed that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you learn of civilian casualties, and if so, what did you do about that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: We found out about our casualties on our side. There were quite a few civilian casualties, and we tried in every conceivable way to remove them from the front line. We did our best, to the best of our ability. As for the Muslim side, when UNPROFOR arrived we had some information to the effect that certain incidents had occurred as far as Muslim civilians are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you asked to testify in any other case before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was 2003. I was called in for an interview in General Galic's case. I was in Belgrade a few times to talk to people from The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how did it happen that you did not testify after all?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Well, probably they didn't like my answers. I mean, it is a fact that during those first days of my interviews there wasn't any pressure, any duress, and as the interview proceeded, there was more and more pressure exerted. They were not happy with some of the answers that I provided to their questions, and once I said, Now, how come you're asking me to provide false testimony against my general with whom I fought for four years? And they said that they had the right to transfer me and to protect me in Canada, America, Europe, that that's no problem, that I should just say what suited them and I didn't accept that, and that's probably the reason why ultimately I did not testify in General Galic's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guzina. At this point in time I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, who are they, the Prosecutor's office or the Defence of Mr. Galic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor's office. As far as I know, it was the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guzina, as you have noted now, your evidence in most part was admitted in -- in writing, in written form, i.e., your statement, in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you'll be

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. West. Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Guzina.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We're going to spend a little bit of time speaking this afternoon, but this will go over to next week. And the first question that I want to ask you regards your area of responsibility. May we have 1D10070, please. I know you provided some maps for the Defence in which you outlined the area in which you operated, and one of those maps is going to come up shortly. Do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And it's -- it's a bit difficult to see, but we see a red line, and it goes around the area of Nedzarici. At the very most northern part of your area of responsibility -- may I ask the usher's assistance please to turn on his monitor so he can mark it. I'd like you to show me where the school of the blind is located, and in a moment you're going to be able to mark on your screen. You can just circle the building, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And you can put a B next to that, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, this is one of the buildings that you noted in paragraph 36 of your statement that was a building of significance in your area of responsibility. You also noted the theology institute. Can you please circle that for me.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And put a T next to at that, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Can you sign and date that, please. Today is the 6th.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Which part of the map?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: In the bottom is fine.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, may I tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document marked by the witness becomes Exhibit P6037, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, sir, at paragraph 44 of your statement -- I see that you have a copy in front of you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: May I use it though?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Yes. I'll refer you to paragraph 44. And in paragraph 44, that's when you speak about a particular incident that we have indicated is incident F7. It happened on May 25th, 1994, and this is an allegation that -- a sniping allegation where the round hit a bus and then ricochetted off the bus and hit two women inside the bus. Do you remember speaking about this incident with the Defence?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we have P01739, please. In a moment on your screen you're going to see a map. This is from the Sarajevo map book. And this is an area that I would suspect you're familiar with. This is Dobrinja; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And if you'd look at the red number 7. Do you see that circle with the number 7 on it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And that's the crossroads of the incident that you spoke about in paragraph 44; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, on this map I think you'll be able to find the theological institute if you look closely. I know you're familiar with this area, but do you see the theological institute on this map?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Point 75, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: That is, and that's fine. You don't need to mark it. Were you aware that at the end of the street, the end of the street where the crossroads were, Bulevar AVNOJ, there was a screen placed there for the purposes of deterring sniper attacks? Were you aware of that information?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, do you concede that your battalion had sniper rifles in its possession?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did your battalion have any sniper rifles in its possession?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And so you received no information about any sniping going on within your battalion. Is that what I should understand?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: I received information about sniping from UNPROFOR -- or, rather, the liaison officers who were in contact with us every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: When you say you received information from UNPROFOR, were they suggesting that sniping was coming out of your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: UNPROFOR officers conveyed it that way. However, the fact is that it was only one side, that is to say the Muslim side, that conveyed this to them. We had not even seen that activity, and after all, we hadn't carried it out to begin with. It was just one-sided. UNPROFOR conveyed it to us, whereas this was conveyed to them by the Muslims and the documentation was from the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And when UNPROFOR approached you with that information, did you tell them you had no sniper rifles in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Specifically in this case, if we're talking about incident F7 --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm not. I'm speaking generally.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Oh, generally. The fact is that in my 1st Battalion there was no need for us to have sniper rifles. You will see where the separation line was in the 1st Battalion. In 90 per cent of all cases, it was just the street. So there was 25 to 30 metres involved only. So in this urban area, a sniper could not operate at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get back to that, but let's go back to my question, which is: When the UNPROFOR approached you and suggested to you that there were allegations -- allegations of sniping coming out of your area of responsibility, did you tell UNPROFOR, We don't have sniper rifles. We are not sniping. Did you deny that you were doing that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Well, of course I denied it, because I know that we did not have any sniper rifles in the area of the 1st Battalion. As a matter of fact, I know that we did not have trained sniper shooters, and I claim that with full responsibility. I claim that with full responsibility, and I stand by that. Now, whether there was a hunting gun or an M-48 with some optics possibly, but sniper rifles, no, we did not have any.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, you just said you had no trained sniper shooters, but you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that even an untrained sniper shooter but somebody who was just a good shot could hit a stationary bus. That seems reasonable, don't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Well, it would be that way sort of.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by that answer. Is it true that somebody who is not necessarily a trained sniper could easily hit a stationary bus?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR GUZINA
utterances.text: Well, if this is not a trained sniper shooter, if he were to fire ten bullets at the bus, maybe one or two would hit the target, but certainly not all ten.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay, we'll leave that there.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I inquire if this is a good time to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guzina, we have to adjourn for the week and resume next week on Tuesday at 9.00, but in the meantime, you are not supposed to discuss with anybody else about your testimony while you are in the course of giving testimony. Do you understand that, sir, Mr. Guzina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
